headline: High: Copilot can read and edit repo context while Authelia has broad egress and OIDC/OAuth surfaces, creating default-risk leakage and action-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot ingests editor buffers and repo context by default, so malicious content in files can influence its outputs. Authelia exposes OAuth/OIDC and ForwardAuth surfaces, but no direct shared channel is documented between the pair. The pathway exists via file content, yet the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Authelia-generated or user-edited content is placed in files that Copilot reads as repo context, THEN prompt-injection risk exists.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits from untrusted file content without human review, THEN the injection can affect code changes.
mitigations: Review Copilot suggestions before accepting edits.
Keep untrusted text out of repo files used as context.
Use separate repos or branches for untrusted inputs.
Disable Workspace-style auto-apply flows for sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-derived instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot reads open buffers and repo context and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, while Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC surfaces. The pair can therefore expose source code or configuration from shared files, but the profiles do not show PHI or secrets handling, so this is leakage of work product rather than confirmed sensitive data.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or credentials are present in editor buffers or repo context, THEN Copilot may transmit them to its vendor API.
IF Authelia configuration files are opened in the same workspace, THEN those contents can also flow into Copilot context.
mitigations: Remove secrets from files before opening them in Copilot.
Use secret-scanning and redaction in the repo.
Limit Copilot to non-sensitive branches or worktrees.
Audit which files are included in editor context.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based context filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write filesystem edits in Workspace and modify repo content, while Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC integration surfaces. They do not both show unrestricted same-dir writes, but they can still contend over shared repository state and generated edits. Uncertainty about the exact orchestration escalates this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Copilot Workspace proposes edits into the same repository that Authelia-related automation also modifies, THEN write conflicts can occur.
IF git state is changed by one agent while the other is preparing edits, THEN stale or conflicting patches can be produced.
mitigations: Use one writer at a time for the repo.
Commit or stash changes before invoking Copilot.
Review and rebase generated patches immediately.
Avoid concurrent automation on the same branch.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared git state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code suggestions and Workspace edits that a human may accept, while Authelia can act as an authentication component whose configuration changes have downstream effects. The pair creates a plausible chain where Copilot-generated changes are treated as authoritative, but the profiles also show human review in Workspace, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated edits are accepted without review, THEN incorrect code or config can propagate downstream.
IF Authelia configuration is derived from those edits, THEN authentication behavior can change unexpectedly.
mitigations: Require code review for Copilot edits.
Test Authelia config changes in staging first.
Diff generated patches against policy checks.
Keep authentication changes in separate PRs.
requires-engineering: add automated validation for generated config.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is open-source and its profile shows no touched data classes, while Copilot is closed-source and processes editor buffers and repo context under GitHub's vendor API. The main compliance issue is a policy mismatch around code/data residency and retention for repository content, but no PHI or regulated data flow is documented, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated or restricted repository content is opened in Copilot, THEN vendor processing may violate local policy.
IF the organization requires on-prem-only handling of source code, THEN Copilot's vendor API use becomes noncompliant.
mitigations: Restrict Copilot to non-regulated repos.
Check vendor/data-processing terms before use.
Mark sensitive repos as Copilot-disabled.
Document retention and residency expectations.
requires-engineering: route restricted projects to an approved local model.
